doc.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Sanctified church, Daddy Grace's church and the tambourine
summary: Talk of the sanctified rule against crossing feet, music from Daddy Grace's church near the Apollo, and the tambourine with the head.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Well let me ask you this. Now they had a little thing that they came up with, the sanctified church. And you know how when the music gets going or the sermon’s good or the choir just got done singing a good number and the folk get to dancing. And now but they said it wasn’t dancing as long as you didn’t cross your feet.
As long as you didn’t pick that one foot up over the other and cross it, then they wouldn’t —

Right, and it says, make the joyful noise unto the Lord. The many times that I used to play the Apollo Theater, the most urgent thing that would happen when the show was over, everybody would come out the stage entrance which was on 126th Street, come around the block to 8th Avenue, past the Braddock Bar and cross the street. On the corner at 125th and 8th, upstairs, was Daddy Grace’s church. And the windows were always open. Now they had saxophone, drum, trombone, guitar, tambourine. If you wanted to hear music, people dancing in the streets down underneath.
And the tambourines with their heads on them right?

Thank you, well, not that little ring. See when I did a tune in 1953 called “Mama He Treats Your Daughter Mean,” I played the tambourine with the head. I notice everybody now, but that tune, the introduction was four bars for nothing [taps] that’s the original

entrance. But all the tambourines they use now they take the head off, put their hands through it, it rings, and it’s simpler. But that tambourine came out of the church and it still does now. You know if you want to hear the greatest, the greatest, what I say the greatest soul searching music, you go to the holiness church, the Pentecostal, you know, that’s where it is. They truly make a joyful noise unto the Lord. And most of your great R&B singers came out of that kind of setting.
